question: Which para-athlete was honoured with the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award by President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan in January 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Praveen Kumar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Praveen Kumar**, the celebrated **para-high jumper**, was conferred with India's highest sporting honor, the **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award**, for the year **2024**.
 
• The prestigious award was presented by **President Droupadi Murmu** during a ceremony held at **Rashtrapati Bhavan** in **January 2025**.
 
• The **21-year-old** athlete from **Noida**, **Uttar Pradesh**, was recognized for his extraordinary performance at the **Paris 2024 Paralympics**, where he clinched the **Gold Medal** in the **Men's High Jump T64** event.
 
• During the **Paris 2024** games, he set a new **Asian Record** by clearing a height of **2.08 meters**, securing his second consecutive Paralympic medal after winning **Silver** at the **Tokyo 2020 Paralympics**.
 
• His selection was recommended by the **National Sports Awards** committee, overseen by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**, making him the only recipient of the **Khel Ratna** for this cycle. ***Hence, the correct answer is Praveen Kumar.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award:**
 
 
• It is the **highest sporting honor** of the Republic of India, awarded annually by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**.
 
• The award was formerly known as the **Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award** before being renamed in **August 2021** in honor of the hockey legend **Major Dhyan Chand**.
 
• Recipients receive a **medallion**, a **certificate**, and a substantial cash prize of **Rs. 25 lakh**.
 
• It is awarded for "spectacular and most outstanding performance in the field of sports over a period of **four years**" at the international level.
 
 
 
• **National Sports Awards:**
 
 
• This umbrella of awards includes the **Arjuna Award** (for consistent outstanding performance), the **Dronacharya Award** (for eminent coaches), and the **Dhyan Chand Award for Lifetime Achievement**.
 
• Traditionally, these awards are presented on **August 29**, which is **National Sports Day**, marking the birth anniversary of **Major Dhyan Chand**, though the ceremony date can be adjusted based on the international sports calendar.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Nominees and Awardees:**
 
 
• **Preeti Pal:** A brilliant **para-athlete** who became the first Indian woman to win **two medals** (both **Bronze**) in track events at a single **Paralympics** (**Paris 2024**). She was honored with the **Arjuna Award** for **2024**.
 
• **Ajeet Singh:** A prominent **para-javelin thrower** who won the **Silver Medal** at the **Paris 2024 Paralympics** in the **F46 category**. He was also a recipient of the **Arjuna Award** in **January 2025**.
 
• **Subhash Rana:** A renowned **shooting coach** who has played a pivotal role in mentoring several **para-shooters** to international success, often associated with the **Dronacharya Award** discussions for his contribution to **Indian para-sports**.
 
 
 
• **Selection Process:**
 
 
• The awardees are selected by a **committee** comprising retired judges, former **Khel Ratna** winners, and sports journalists appointed by the **Government of India**.
 
• The performance of athletes in the **Olympic/Paralympic Games**, **Asian Games**, and **Commonwealth Games** carries the highest weightage in the selection criteria.
